BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p26/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p26/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p26/r4.claim: The Meccan disbelievers called Muhammad a poet, but God did not teach him poetry and it did not come naturally.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p26/r4.anchor: قال الكلبي: إن كفار مكة قالوا: إن محمدا شاعر، وما يقوله شعر

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p26/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p26/r5.speaker: الحسن
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p26/r5.claim: The Prophet recited a line in a variant order; Abū Bakr corrected the poet’s wording, and he and ʿUmar testified this confirmed his truthfulness.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p26/r5.anchor: بهذا البيت: كفى بالإسلام والشيب للمرء ناهيا

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p26/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p26/r6.speaker: عائشة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p26/r6.claim: ʿĀʾisha said the Prophet sometimes recited verse by ʿAbd Allāh ibn Rawāḥa, including a line about unexpected news.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p26/r6.anchor: كان يتمثل من شعر عبد الله بن رواحة

BAYDAWI-FULL:36:68-69/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:36:68-69/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:36:68-69/r3.claim: God did not teach Muhammad poetry: the Quran is neither metrically rhymed nor like poetry in meaning and imaginative appeals; God's ability to reverse aging shows His power to darken and transform too.
BAYDAWI-FULL:36:68-69/r3.anchor: فإنه لا يماثله لفظا ولا معنى لأنه غير مقفى ولا موزون

BAYDAWI-FULL:36:68-69/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:36:68-69/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:36:68-69/r4.claim: The Prophet's occasional rhyming lines were spontaneous, not composed as poetry; al-Khalil did not count shortened rajaz meter as poetry.
BAYDAWI-FULL:36:68-69/r4.anchor: اتفاقي من غير تكلف وقصد منه إلى ذلك، وقد يقع مثله كثيرا

BAYDAWI-FULL:36:68-69/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:36:68-69/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:36:68-69/r5.claim: The verb is also reported with short vowels on the two bāʾs and no lengthening of the first tāʾ; the pronoun may refer to the Quran rather than Muhammad.
BAYDAWI-FULL:36:68-69/r5.anchor: هذا وقد روي أنه حرك الباءين وكسر التاء الأولى بلا إشباع

BAYDAWI-FULL:36:68-69/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:36:68-69/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:36:68-69/r6.claim: The Quran is a reminder and a clear heavenly book recited in places of worship; its miraculous character shows it is not human speech.

BIQAI-FULL:v6p277/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p277/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p277/r8.claim: The Prophet's lack of poetry is evidence against his opponents: he passed childhood and youth without composing a verse, though poetic talent cannot ordinarily arise after the age when faculties plateau.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p277/r8.anchor: بيت شعر ما يرى لكم ولأمثالكم فيه من المفاخرة

BIQAI-FULL:v6p279/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p279/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p279/r1.claim: Poetry requires artificial adherence to meter and rhyme that can distort meaning; God did not teach the Prophet this inferior craft but gave him eloquence and graceful, forceful expression in any form.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p279/r1.anchor: لا يليق بجنابنا لأنه لا يفرح به إلا من يريد ترويج كلامه

BIQAI-FULL:v6p279/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p279/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p279/r2.claim: The Prophet's wisdom and concise, noble speech came through inspiration and Gabriel's instruction; he chose the easier of two options unless it involved sin or severing kinship.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p279/r2.anchor: ثم بما ألقاه إليه جبريل عليه السلام مما أمرنا له به من جوامع الكلم

BIQAI-FULL:v6p279/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p279/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p279/r3.claim: A cited line in al-Ḥamāsa is attributed to an unnamed man of Banū Qurayʿ; the poem contrasts wealth with poverty and honor with disgrace.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p279/r3.anchor: عزاه في الحماسة في أوائل باب الأدب إلى رجل من بني قريع لم يسمه

BIQAI-FULL:v6p279/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p279/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p279/r4.claim: Wealth and poverty are not innate traits: a vigorous poor youth may become rich in old age, while a wealthy person may have blameworthy character and a poor person admirable morals.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p279/r4.anchor: كثيرا ما رأينا من فاته الغنى شابا جلدا وناله شيخا ضعيفا

BIQAI-FULL:v6p279/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p279/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p279/r5.claim: Muruwwa means humanity and praiseworthy conduct; one who possesses it by nature practices it young, while a person lacking it cannot acquire it merely by growing older.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p279/r5.anchor: المروءة هي الإنسانية , وهي كل أمر هنيء حميد المغبة جميل العاقبة

DURR-FULL:v7p70/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p70/r4.speaker: السدي
DURR-FULL:v7p70/r4.claim: Al-Suddi says the statement that the Prophet was not taught poetry refers to Muhammad.
DURR-FULL:v7p70/r4.anchor: عن السدي رضي الله عنه في قوله {وما علمناه الشعر} قال: محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

DURR-FULL:v7p70/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p70/r5.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v7p70/r5.claim: Qatada says God protected Muhammad from poetry; the reminder is the Qurʾan, the living person has a living heart and sight, and the decree falls on disbelievers for their evil deeds.
DURR-FULL:v7p70/r5.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله {وما علمناه الشعر وما ينبغي له} قال: محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم عصمه الله من ذلك

DURR-FULL:v7p70/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p70/r6.speaker: عائشة
DURR-FULL:v7p70/r6.claim: Aisha says poetry was the Prophet’s most disliked speech, though he sometimes quoted a line with its beginning and ending reversed; when corrected he said he was not a poet. She also reports his use of a line by Tarafa when uncertain about news.
DURR-FULL:v7p70/r6.anchor: عن عائشة رضي الله عنها قالت: كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا استراب الخبر تمثل ببيت طرفة

DURR-FULL:v7p70/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p70/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v7p70/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas says the Prophet would quote the same poetic line about news coming from an unexpected source.
DURR-FULL:v7p70/r7.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما قال: كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يتمثل من الأشعار

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p460#4/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p460#4/r12.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p460#4/r12.claim: The statement that Muhammad was not taught poetry rejects the disbelievers' claim that he was a poet and that the Quran was poetry; he did not compose or meter verse.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p460#4/r12.anchor: ثم أخبر تعالى عن حال نبيه محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم ورد قول من قال من الكفرة إنه شاعر، وإن القرآن شعر

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p589/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p589/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p589/r1.claim: He cites a fragment from an unnamed Arab poet's poem in al-Ḥamāsa; the excerpt supplies no further gloss.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p589/r1.anchor: من رجال أعزة … علينا وهم كانوا أعق وأظلما

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p589/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p589/r2.speaker: عائشة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p589/r2.claim: When news was delayed, the Prophet quoted a hemistich by Ṭarafa; Aḥmad and al-Nasāʾī transmit it, and al-Tirmidhī grades it ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p589/r2.anchor: عن عائشة، رضي الله عنها، قالت: كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا استراث الخبر، تمثل فيه ببيت طرفة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p589/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p589/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p589/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās also reports the Prophet quoting the same line from Ṭarafa's famous Muʿallaqa; another version is related from ʿĀʾisha.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p589/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يتمثل من الأشعار

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p589/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p589/r4.speaker: عائشة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p589/r4.claim: A report says the Prophet composed only one line, a hopeful saying; al-Mizzī calls this report objectionable because its transmitters are unknown to him.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p589/r4.anchor: عن عائشة، رضي الله عنها، قالت: ما جمع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بيت شعر قط

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p589/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p589/r5.speaker: عائشة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p589/r5.claim: Another report says poetry was the Prophet's most disliked speech, though he sometimes reversed a line's halves and said he was no poet; al-Bukhārī corrects the wording in the report.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p589/r5.anchor: عن قتادة: قيل لعائشة: هل كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يتمثل بشيء من الشعر

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p590/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p590/r1.speaker: قتادة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p590/r1.claim: Qatāda reports ʿĀʾisha's account that the Prophet quoted Ṭarafa but reversed the line's wording; Abū Bakr corrected him, and he said he was no poet and poetry was not fitting for him.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p590/r1.anchor: عن قتادة: بلغني أن عائشة سئلت: هل كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يتمثل بشيء من الشعر

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p590/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p590/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p590/r2.claim: Authentic reports show the Prophet voicing lines by ʿAbd Allāh ibn Rawāḥa while joining the Companions at the Trench, the words matching their work-song.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p590/r2.anchor: ثبت في الصحيحين أنه، عليه الصلاة والسلام، تمثل يوم حفر الخندق بأبيات عبد الله بن رواحة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p590/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p590/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p590/r3.claim: At Ḥunayn the Prophet said he was the Prophet and son of ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib; this and other metrical utterances happened without intending poetry.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p590/r3.anchor: وكذلك ثبت أنه قال يوم حنين وهو راكب البغلة، يقدم بها في نحور العدو

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p590/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p590/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p590/r4.claim: When he injured his finger in a cave, he uttered a metrical line; such accidental speech does not contradict that he was not taught poetry.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p590/r4.anchor: عن جندب بن عبد الله قال: كنا مع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في غار فنكبت أصبعه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p590/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p590/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p590/r5.claim: God taught the Prophet the inimitable Qur'an rather than poetry; claims that it was poetry, soothsaying, fabrication, or magic are false, and his nature rejected poetry as craft.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p590/r5.anchor: فإن الله تعالى إنما علمه القرآن العظيم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p591/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p591/r1.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p591/r1.claim: A report unique to Abū Dāwūd says the Prophet did not care if he received an antidote, wore an amulet, or composed poetry himself.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p591/r1.anchor: سمعت عبد الله بن عمرو يقول

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p591/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p591/r2.speaker: عائشة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p591/r2.claim: ʿĀʾisha says poetry was the Prophet's most disliked speech; she also says he favored concise, comprehensive prayers.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p591/r2.anchor: عن أبي نوفل قال: سألت عائشة: أكان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يتسامع عنده الشعر

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p591/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p591/r3.speaker: أبو هريرة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p591/r3.claim: A Prophetic report says a belly full of pus is better than one full of poetry; this route is unique to Abū Dāwūd and its chain meets the Ṣaḥīḥayn's standard, though they did not include it.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p591/r3.anchor: عن أبي هريرة، رضي الله عنه، عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: "لأن يمتلئ جوف أحدكم قيحا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p591/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p591/r4.speaker: شداد بن أوس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p591/r4.claim: A rare report says composing a line of poetry after the late-night prayer makes that night's prayer unacceptable; Ibn Kathīr interprets this as composing, not reciting, poetry.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p591/r4.anchor: عن شداد بن أوس قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "من قرض بيت شعر

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p591/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p591/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p591/r5.claim: Some poetry is commendable, such as Muslim poets' satire of polytheists and poetry of wisdom, admonition, and good manners.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p591/r5.anchor: على أن الشعر فيه ما هو مشروع، وهو هجاء المشركين الذي كان يتعاطاه شعراء الإسلام

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p591/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p591/r6.speaker: أمية بن أبي الصلت
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p591/r6.claim: The Prophet said of Umayya ibn Abī al-Ṣalt, whose poetry includes wisdom, that his poetry believed while his heart disbelieved.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p591/r6.anchor: ومنهم أمية بن أبي الصلت الذي قال فيه النبي الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p591/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p591/r7.speaker: صحابي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p591/r7.claim: A Companion recited one hundred lines of Umayya's poetry to the Prophet, who encouraged him to continue after each line.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p591/r7.anchor: وقد أنشد بعض الصحابة منه للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم مائة بيت

JISHUMI:v8p5896/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5896/r7.speaker: أبو جعفر، نافع، ابن عامر، يعقوب
JISHUMI:v8p5896/r7.claim: These readers use the tāʾ form لتنذر, addressing the Prophet; others use a yāʾ form referring to the Qur'an or Book, with one view taking it as the Prophet.
JISHUMI:v8p5896/r7.anchor: قرأ أبو جعفر ونافع وابن عامر ويعقوب: لتنذر بالتاء على الخطاب للرسول

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p29/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p29/r8.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p29/r8.claim: The Qur'an God taught is not poetry, or He did not teach His Messenger to compose it.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p29/r8.anchor: ليس الذي علمناه من القرآن شعرا . الثاني : أي لم نعلم رسولنا أن يقول الشعر

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p29/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p29/r9.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p29/r9.claim: It is not fitting for the Messenger to compose poetry or God to teach it to him.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p29/r9.anchor: وما ينبغي له أن يقول شعرا . الثاني : وما ينبغي لنا أن نعلمه شعرا

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p29/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p29/r10.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p29/r10.claim: The Qur'an may be taught as reminder and clear recitation, or the recitation itself is called that.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p29/r10.anchor: إن علمناه إلا ذكرا وقرآنا مبينا . الثاني : إن هذا الذي يتلوه عليكم إلا ذكر وقرآن مبين

MUQATIL:36:66-69/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:36:66-69/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:36:66-69/r4.claim: The verse answered Uqba ibn Abi Muayt and companions who said the Quran was poetry: the Prophet was not taught poetry and it does not suit him.
MUQATIL:36:66-69/r4.anchor: { وما علمناه الشعر } نزلت فى عقبة ابن أبى معيط وأصحابه، قالوا: إن القرآن شعر { وما ينبغي له } أن يعلمه

MUQATIL:36:66-69/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:36:66-69/r5.speaker: author
MUQATIL:36:66-69/r5.claim: The Quran is a reminder or reflection and a clear recitation.
MUQATIL:36:66-69/r5.anchor: { إن هو } يعنى القرآن { إلا ذكر } تفكر { وقرآن مبين } [آية: 69] بين.

ZAJJAJ:v4p293/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p293/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p293/r4.claim: The Prophet was not taught poetry, but this does not mean he never recited a poetic line; he is no poet, and the Qur'an is unlike human speech and Arab meters.
ZAJJAJ:v4p293/r4.anchor: إنما يوجب هذا أن يكون النبي عليه السلام ليس بشاعر، وأن يكون القرآن

ZAJJAJ:v4p293/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p293/r5.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p293/r5.claim: The Qur'an is a lasting miraculous sign proving the Prophet's prophethood.
ZAJJAJ:v4p293/r5.anchor: والقرآن آية معجزة تدل على أن نبوة النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم -

TABATABAI:36:66-69/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:36:66-69/r10.speaker: author
TABATABAI:36:66-69/r10.claim: The denial that Muhammad was taught poetry returns to the surah's opening affirmation that he is a messenger and his book is revealed remembrance, not poetry.
TABATABAI:36:66-69/r10.anchor: عطف ورجوع إلى ما تقدم في صدر السورة من تصديق رسالة النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

TABATABAI:36:66-83/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:36:66-83/r1.speaker: أبو بكر عن النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
TABATABAI:36:66-83/r1.claim: Reports describe the Prophet quoting a poetic line about the days revealing what one did not know; Abu Bakr corrected his wording, and the Prophet said he was not a poet and should not be one.
TABATABAI:36:66-83/r1.anchor: فجعل يقول ويأتيك من لم تزود بالأخبار فيقول أبو بكر ليس هكذا يارسول الله

TABATABAI:36:66-83/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:36:66-83/r2.speaker: الحسن وعائشة
TABATABAI:36:66-83/r2.claim: Al-Durr al-Manthur also transmits reports from al-Hasan and Aisha about the Prophet reciting lines of poetry.
TABATABAI:36:66-83/r2.anchor: وروى في الدر المنثور الخبرين عن الحسن وعائشة كما رواه

TABATABAI:36:66-83/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:36:66-83/r3.speaker: مجمع البيان
TABATABAI:36:66-83/r3.claim: On 'I am the prophet, no lie; I am the son of Abd al-Muttalib,' some say it is not poetry, while others call its meter accidental and unintentional; al-Tabataba'i says rejecting the report is easier than denying the line is poetry or deliberate verse.
TABATABAI:36:66-83/r3.anchor: فأما قوله أنا النبي لا كذب أنا ابن عبد المطلب فقد قال قوم إن هذا ليس بشعر

TABRISI:36:66-69/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:36:66-69/r10.speaker: author
TABRISI:36:66-69/r10.claim: God did not teach Muhammad the craft or composition of poetry, and poetry was not fitting for him.

TABRISI:36:66-70/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:36:66-70/r1.speaker: الحسن
TABRISI:36:66-70/r1.claim: Hasan relates that the Prophet recited a line in altered order; Abu Bakr corrected it, and the incident demonstrated that the Prophet had not been taught poetry.
TABRISI:36:66-70/r1.anchor: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كان يتمثل بهذا البيت

TABRISI:36:66-70/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:36:66-70/r2.speaker: عائشة
TABRISI:36:66-70/r2.claim: Aisha reports another occasion when the Prophet reshaped a line; Abu Bakr corrected him, and the Prophet said he was not a poet and poetry was not fitting for him.
TABRISI:36:66-70/r2.anchor: ليس هكذا يا رسول الله فيقول: إني لست بشاعر

TABRISI:36:66-70/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:36:66-70/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:36:66-70/r3.claim: The phrase I am the Prophet without a lie, son of Abd al-Muttalib was either not poetry or an accidental utterance rather than intentional composition.
TABRISI:36:66-70/r3.anchor: فقد قال قوم: إن هذا ليس بشعر

TABRISI:36:66-70/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:36:66-70/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:36:66-70/r4.claim: Another interpretation is that the Quran was not taught as poetry and its composition is not poetic; the Prophet did hear poetry and encouraged it.
TABRISI:36:66-70/r4.anchor: وما علمناه الشعر بتعليم القرآن وما ينبغى للقرآن أن يكون شعرا

TABRISI:36:66-70/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:36:66-70/r5.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
TABRISI:36:66-70/r5.claim: The Prophet told Hassan ibn Thabit that he would remain supported by the Holy Spirit while defending the community with his tongue.
TABRISI:36:66-70/r5.anchor: لا تزال يا حسان مؤيدا بروح القدس ما نصرتنا بلسانك

THALABI:v8p135/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p135/r6.speaker: author
THALABI:v8p135/r6.claim: God did not teach the Prophet poetry and poetry was not appropriate for him because it could produce doubt.
THALABI:v8p135/r6.anchor: وما علمناه الشعر وما ينبغي له لأنه يورث الشبهة

THALABI:v8p135#2/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p135#2/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v8p135#2/r1.claim: The report depicts the Prophet repeating a poetic line with its word order reversed; Abu Bakr corrected him, and he denied being a poet.
THALABI:v8p135#2/r1.anchor: أتجعل نهبي ونهب العبيد بين الأقرع وعيينة

THALABI:v8p135#2/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p135#2/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
THALABI:v8p135#2/r2.claim: Al-Hasan reports that the Prophet quoted a verse with words transposed; Abu Bakr corrected him, and the Prophet affirmed that poetry was not his proper calling.
THALABI:v8p135#2/r2.anchor: عن الحسن أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كان يتمثل بهذا البيت

THALABI:v8p135#2/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p135#2/r3.speaker: عائشة
THALABI:v8p135#2/r3.claim: Aisha said poetry was the speech most disliked by the Prophet; he only recited a line by Tarafa, misplacing its ending, then said he was no poet.
THALABI:v8p135#2/r3.anchor: عائشة سئلت هل كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يتمثل بشيء من الشعر

THALABI:v8p135#2/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p135#2/r4.speaker: author
THALABI:v8p135#2/r4.claim: The reading with the second-person verb is used by most Medinan, Syrian, and Basran readers except Abu Amr; the other reading refers to the Quran, while the first addresses the Prophet.
THALABI:v8p135#2/r4.anchor: التاء للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم والياء للقرآن

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:36:66-70/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:36:66-70/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:36:66-70/r4.claim: God did not teach Muhammad poetry, nor is it easy for him; what he brought is only a reminder and clear Qur'an.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:36:66-70/r4.anchor: { وما علمناه الشعر } لم نعلم محمدا صلى الله عليه وسلم قول الشعر { وما ينبغي له }

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p817#2/r6.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p817#2/r6.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p817#2/r6.claim: The statement that the Prophet was not taught poetry refers to the Prophet.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p817#2/r6.anchor: قوله عز وجل: {وما علمناه الشعر} [يس: 69] ، يعني: النبي عليه السلام.

ELMALILI:36:68-76/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:36:68-76/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:36:68-76/r3.claim: The Qur'an is not poetry in form: its arrangement has neither the meter nor rhyme of poetry.
ELMALILI:36:68-76/r3.anchor: Kur’ân’ın nazmında şiir nazmının vezn ü kāfiyesi yoktur.

ELMALILI:36:68-76/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:36:68-76/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:36:68-76/r4.claim: Poetry can manipulate feeling through imagined fancies, conjectural comparisons, and emotional tricks regardless of truth; the Qur'an instead guides to truth through wisdom, law, knowledge, and certainty.
ELMALILI:36:68-76/r4.anchor: şiir, hakikat olup olmadığı aranmaksızın hoşlandırmak veya tiksindirmek, coşturmak veya küstürmek gibi hisleri gıcıklayan muhayyel kuruntulara, vehmî kıyaslara, hissiyyât oyunlarına râci‘dir.

ELMALILI:36:68-76/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:36:68-76/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:36:68-76/r5.claim: The Qur'an is divine guidance to the straight path, carrying wisdom and law, the light of knowledge, and a guide to certainty.
ELMALILI:36:68-76/r5.anchor: Hakk’ın sırât-ı müstakīmine irşad eden hikem ve ahkâm ile irfan nûru, îkān rehberi bir yâdigâr-ı ilâhîdir.

ELMALILI:36:68-76/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:36:68-76/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:36:68-76/r6.claim: Disbelievers persist in calling the Qur'an poetry to portray the Prophet as a poet; Elmalılı cites 26:224 and says poetry suits neither prophethood nor the Qur'an.
ELMALILI:36:68-76/r6.anchor: kâfirlerin birçokları onu bir şiir gibi mülâhaza etmek ve ettirmekte ısrar ettikleri

ELMALILI:36:68-76/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:36:68-76/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:36:68-76/r7.claim: The Qur'an is remembrance and admonition from God.
ELMALILI:36:68-76/r7.anchor: mahza Allah tarafından bir va‘z u irşad

ELMALILI:36:68-76/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:36:68-76/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:36:68-76/r8.claim: It is a clear Qur'an, the word of God to be recited in acts of worship and places of worship.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p371/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p371/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p371/r6.claim: The closing section resumes the opening themes of monotheism and the Hereafter and assures the Prophet that he awakens the morally living, not the dead-hearted.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p371/r6.anchor: what was discussed in the opening one is take up again in a different style

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p408/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p408/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p408/r6.claim: The sūrah closes by returning to its opening theme: the wise Qur'an validates the Prophet's mission and benefits Arabs, though only spiritually vital people believe.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p408/r6.anchor: the sūrah began with an oath sworn by the Qur’ān replete with wisdom.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p408/r7.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p408/r7.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p408/r7.claim: The closing passage again validates the Qur'an's claims, beginning by refuting hypocrites who call it poetry and the Prophet a poet.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p408/r7.anchor: Here too, in the concluding section of the sūrah, this sequence can be seen in a new style.

SIBAWAYH:اعلمأنكلاسممعالهاءثلاثةأحرفأوأك.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:اعلمأنكلاسممعالهاءثلاثةأحرفأوأك.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:اعلمأنكلاسممعالهاءثلاثةأحرفأوأك.claim: In vocative use, names of three or more letters ending in feminine hāʾ usually drop it, whether proper names or common nouns; shorter examples include شاة and ثبة.
SIBAWAYH:اعلمأنكلاسممعالهاءثلاثةأحرفأوأك.anchor: فأما ما كان اسما غالبا فنحو قولك يا سلم أقبل

SIBAWAYH:اعلمأنكلاسممعالهاءثلاثةأحرفأوأك.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:اعلمأنكلاسممعالهاءثلاثةأحرفأوأك.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:اعلمأنكلاسممعالهاءثلاثةأحرفأوأك.claim: Some Arabs retain feminine hāʾ in the vocative, saying يا سلمة; even speakers who delete it in connected speech restore it at pause to show the final consonant's vowel.
SIBAWAYH:اعلمأنكلاسممعالهاءثلاثةأحرفأوأك.anchor: واعلم أن ناسا من العرب يثبتون الهاء فيقولون يا سلمة

SIBAWAYH:اعلمأنكلاسممعالهاءثلاثةأحرفأوأك.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:اعلمأنكلاسممعالهاءثلاثةأحرفأوأك.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:اعلمأنكلاسممعالهاءثلاثةأحرفأوأك.claim: At pause, hāʾ is retained in forms like يا سلمة and ارمه to avoid leaving the deleted consonant unvocalized; poetic meter can license its omission because rhyme length replaces it.
SIBAWAYH:اعلمأنكلاسممعالهاءثلاثةأحرفأوأك.anchor: إذا وقفوا قالوا يا سلمة ويا طلحة

SIBAWAYH:اعلمأنكلاسممعالهاءثلاثةأحرفأوأك.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:اعلمأنكلاسممعالهاءثلاثةأحرفأوأك.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:اعلمأنكلاسممعالهاءثلاثةأحرفأوأك.claim: Vocative hāʾ is more readily deleted than other letters because it has no replacement in this position, whereas it becomes tāʾ elsewhere; a reliable Arab said يا حرمل for يا حرمله.
SIBAWAYH:اعلمأنكلاسممعالهاءثلاثةأحرفأوأك.anchor: يا حرمل يريد يا حرمله كما قال بعضهم إرم

SIBAWAYH:اعلمأنكلاسممعالهاءثلاثةأحرفأوأك.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:اعلمأنكلاسممعالهاءثلاثةأحرفأوأك.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:اعلمأنكلاسممعالهاءثلاثةأحرفأوأك.claim: Feminine hāʾ does not license deleting preceding added letters that would otherwise remain; examples include طائفية to يا طائفي and مرجانة to يا مرجان, with analogous treatment of root letters.
SIBAWAYH:اعلمأنكلاسممعالهاءثلاثةأحرفأوأك.anchor: واعلم أن هاء التأنيث إذا كانت بعد حرف زائد لو لم تكن بعده حذف

SIBAWAYH:لأنهلايجوزللاأنتعملفيمعرفةكمالا.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:لأنهلايجوزللاأنتعملفيمعرفةكمالا.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:لأنهلايجوزللاأنتعملفيمعرفةكمالا.claim: لا, like رب, cannot govern a definite noun; treating ولا العباس as governed by لا would require the same construction with رب, and لا غلام لك وأخوه illustrates the contrast.
SIBAWAYH:لأنهلايجوزللاأنتعملفيمعرفةكمالا.anchor: لأنه لا يجوز للا أن تعمل في معرفة كما لا يجوز ذلك لرب

SIBAWAYH:لأنهلايجوزللاأنتعملفيمعرفةكمالا.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:لأنهلايجوزللاأنتعملفيمعرفةكمالا.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:لأنهلايجوزللاأنتعملفيمعرفةكمالا.claim: On the pattern كل شاة وسخلتها بدرهم, coordination after لا رجل لك takes accusative وأخاه, understood as لا رجل لك وأخا له.
SIBAWAYH:لأنهلايجوزللاأنتعملفيمعرفةكمالا.anchor: فأما من قال كل شاة وسخلتها بدرهم

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمالايجوزفيهمنبناتالحرفين.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمالايجوزفيهمنبناتالحرفين.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمالايجوزفيهمنبناتالحرفين.claim: Nisba forms from two-radical nouns restore the lost final root consonant, as in أبوي, أخوي and حموي; dual and plural forms expose that root, so restoration is stronger in nisba.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمالايجوزفيهمنبناتالحرفين.anchor: وذلك قولك في أب أبوي وفي أخ أخوي وفي حم حموي ولا يجوز إلا ذا

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمالايجوزفيهمنبناتالحرفين.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمالايجوزفيهمنبناتالحرفين.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمالايجوزفيهمنبناتالحرفين.claim: Some speakers treat هن like أب, saying هنوان and هنوات, then derive هنوي; سنة likewise has the regular سنوي, while an hāʾ-root analysis gives سنيهة and سانهت, like شفة.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمالايجوزفيهمنبناتالحرفين.anchor: من العرب من يقول هذا هنوك ورأيت هناك

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمالايجوزفيهمنبناتالحرفين.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمالايجوزفيهمنبناتالحرفين.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمالايجوزفيهمنبناتالحرفين.claim: The poem's عضوات supports deriving عضوي; another dialect treats عضة as hāʾ-final and says عضيهة, like شفة.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمالايجوزفيهمنبناتالحرفين.anchor: عضيهة يجعلها من بنات الهاء بمنزلة شفة

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمالايجوزفيهمنبناتالحرفين.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمالايجوزفيهمنبناتالحرفين.speaker: الخليل
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمالايجوزفيهمنبناتالحرفين.claim: Al-Khalīl derives أخوي: the feminine tāʾ disappears in pluralization, exposing the root; nisba likewise removes tāʾ and restores the root consonant. Yūnus's أختي is not analogical.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمالايجوزفيهمنبناتالحرفين.anchor: قلت أخوي هكذا ينبغي له أن يكون على القياس

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمالايجوزفيهمنبناتالحرفين.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمالايجوزفيهمنبناتالحرفين.speaker: يونس
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمالايجوزفيهمنبناتالحرفين.claim: Yūnus instead says أختي, which Sībawayh explicitly calls non-analogical.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمالايجوزفيهمنبناتالحرفين.anchor: وأما يونس فيقول أختي وليس بقياس

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتحقيرماحذفمنهولايردفيالت.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتحقيرماحذفمنهولايردفيالت.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتحقيرماحذفمنهولايردفيالت.claim: Diminutives do not restore a deleted root consonant: the remainder already fits a diminutive pattern, and the missing element is not an added suffix like tāʾ or feminine hāʾ.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتحقيرماحذفمنهولايردفيالت.anchor: من قبل أن ما بقي إذا حقر يكون على مثال المحقر

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتحقيرماحذفمنهولايردفيالت.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتحقيرماحذفمنهولايردفيالت.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتحقيرماحذفمنهولايردفيالت.claim: Thus ميت gives مييت from ميت after deletion of the middle radical, and هار gives هوير from هائر after deletion of hamza; both missing elements substitute for the middle radical.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتحقيرماحذفمنهولايردفيالت.anchor: فمن ذلك قولك في ميت مييت وإنما الأصل ميت غير أنك حذفت العين

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتحقيرماحذفمنهولايردفيالت.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتحقيرماحذفمنهولايردفيالت.speaker: يونس
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتحقيرماحذفمنهولايردفيالت.claim: Yūnus reports هويئر, a diminutive of the full هائر rather than truncated هار; Sībawayh says not to generalize such irregular forms without further Arabic evidence.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتحقيرماحذفمنهولايردفيالت.anchor: وزعم يونس أن ناسا يقولون هويئر على مثال هويعر

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتحقيرماحذفمنهولايردفيالت.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتحقيرماحذفمنهولايردفيالت.speaker: أبو عمرو
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتحقيرماحذفمنهولايردفيالت.claim: Yūnus reports Abū ʿAmr's forms مريء and يريء for مر and يري, with hamza as in مريع and the yāʾ of قاض; by this analysis he should also say مييت and أنيس.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتحقيرماحذفمنهولايردفيالت.anchor: كان يقول في مر مريء مثل مريع وفي يري يريء

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتحقيرماحذفمنهولايردفيالت.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتحقيرماحذفمنهولايردفيالت.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتحقيرماحذفمنهولايردفيالت.claim: The same no-restoration rule gives يضيع for a man called بيضع and خيير منك or شرير منك for خير منك and شر منك; augmentations are not restored.

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتمييزبناتالأربعةوالخمسةم.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتمييزبناتالأربعةوالخمسةم.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتمييزبناتالأربعةوالخمسةم.claim: جعفر is a four-radical form and سفرجل a five-radical form; neither has extra letters or deletion.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتمييزبناتالأربعةوالخمسةم.anchor: فأما جعفر فمن بنات الأربعة لا زيادة فيه لأنه ليس شيء من أمهات الزوائد

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتمييزبناتالأربعةوالخمسةم.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتمييزبناتالأربعةوالخمسةم.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتمييزبناتالأربعةوالخمسةم.claim: Treating any radical in جعفر, غلفق, or فرزدق as an augment yields implausible patterns and makes original letters into augments.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتمييزبناتالأربعةوالخمسةم.anchor: الفاء فهو ينبغي له أن يقول إنه فعلر وفعفل وينبغي له إن جاء الأولى زائدة

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتمييزبناتالأربعةوالخمسةم.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتمييزبناتالأربعةوالخمسةم.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتمييزبناتالأربعةوالخمسةم.claim: فعْلَل is not a form for a word with no doubled radical; it is valid only as a template.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتمييزبناتالأربعةوالخمسةم.anchor: ولا تقول فعلل ولا فعلل لأنك لم تضعف شيئا وإنما يجوز هذا

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابفعلمنفوعلتمنقلتوفيعلتمنب.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابفعلمنفوعلتمنقلتوفيعلتمنب.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابفعلمنفوعلتمنقلتوفيعلتمنب.claim: Defective roots in فوعلت and فيعلت form قوول and بويع with lengthening, parallel to فاعلت.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابفعلمنفوعلتمنقلتوفيعلتمنب.anchor: قد قوول وقد بويع في فوعلت وفيعلت

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابفعلمنفوعلتمنقلتوفيعلتمنب.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابفعلمنفوعلتمنقلتوفيعلتمنب.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابفعلمنفوعلتمنقلتوفيعلتمنب.claim: The wāw and yāʾ of these forms are augment letters like alif, since they can occur without a homorganic letter after them and without obligatory doubling.

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابفعلمنفوعلتمنقلتوفيعلتمنب.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابفعلمنفوعلتمنقلتوفيعلتمنب.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابفعلمنفوعلتمنقلتوفيعلتمنب.claim: فعولت and فعيلت are lengthened rather than geminated because their added letters remain distinct, as in جهورت.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابفعلمنفوعلتمنقلتوفيعلتمنب.anchor: ولم تجعل هذا بمنزلة العينين في حولت وزيلت

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابفعلمنفوعلتمنقلتوفيعلتمنب.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابفعلمنفوعلتمنقلتوفيعلتمنب.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابفعلمنفوعلتمنقلتوفيعلتمنب.claim: In بووع, the yāʾ of بويع changes to wāw under the preceding ḍamma, as in فعللت.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابفعلمنفوعلتمنقلتوفيعلتمنب.anchor: قلبت ياء بويع واوا للضمة كما فعلت ذلك في فعللت

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابفعلمنفوعلتمنقلتوفيعلتمنب.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابفعلمنفوعلتمنقلتوفيعلتمنب.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابفعلمنفوعلتمنقلتوفيعلتمنب.claim: In افعوعلت from سرت, a quiescent wāw before yāʾ becomes yāʾ, giving اسييرت.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابفعلمنفوعلتمنقلتوفيعلتمنب.anchor: تقول في افعوعلت من سرت اسييرت تقلب الواو ياء لأنها ساكنة

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابفعلمنفوعلتمنقلتوفيعلتمنب.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابفعلمنفوعلتمنقلتوفيعلتمنب.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابفعلمنفوعلتمنقلتوفيعلتمنب.claim: Where the wāw is not followed by yāʾ, it remains wāw, as in اسيويرت, by analogy with اغدودن.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابفعلمنفوعلتمنقلتوفيعلتمنب.anchor: فإذا قلت فعلت قلت اسيويرت لأن هذه الواو قد تقع وليست بعدها ياء

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابفعلمنفوعلتمنقلتوفيعلتمنب.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابفعلمنفوعلتمنقلتوفيعلتمنب.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابفعلمنفوعلتمنقلتوفيعلتمنب.claim: The hypothetical form of اليوم is avoided because its inflection would bring together a weak consonant and a yāʾ bearing ḍamma, an especially heavy sequence.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابفعلمنفوعلتمنقلتوفيعلتمنب.anchor: ياءان في إحداهما ضمة مع المعتل

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابفعلمنفوعلتمنقلتوفيعلتمنب.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابفعلمنفوعلتمنقلتوفيعلتمنب.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابفعلمنفوعلتمنقلتوفيعلتمنب.claim: Related forms such as واوة, ويح, and ويل are analogized to اليوم and assigned hypothetical roots despite being unused, because their forms are heavy.

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابفعلمنفوعلتمنقلتوفيعلتمنب.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابفعلمنفوعلتمنقلتوفيعلتمنب.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابفعلمنفوعلتمنقلتوفيعلتمنب.claim: Forms from اليوم include أيمت and retain wāw in related patterns such as أووم, يووم, and مووم.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابفعلمنفوعلتمنقلتوفيعلتمنب.anchor: لأن الياء لا يلزمها أن تكون بعدها ياء

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابفعلمنفوعلتمنقلتوفيعلتمنب.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابفعلمنفوعلتمنقلتوفيعلتمنب.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابفعلمنفوعلتمنقلتوفيعلتمنب.claim: In أفعل, مفعل, and يفعل forms from اليوم, the wāw remains in أووم, يووم, and مووم because a yāʾ need not be followed by another yāʾ.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابفعلمنفوعلتمنقلتوفيعلتمنب.anchor: لأن الياء لا يلزمها أن تكون بعدها ياء

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابفعلمنفوعلتمنقلتوفيعلتمنب.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابفعلمنفوعلتمنقلتوفيعلتمنب.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابفعلمنفوعلتمنقلتوفيعلتمنب.claim: The broken plural of أيم is أيائم with hamza, since this form is weakened like سيد and follows أول.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابفعلمنفوعلتمنقلتوفيعلتمنب.anchor: فقلت أيائم لأنها اعتلت ههنا كما اعتلت في سيد

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابفعلمنفوعلتمنقلتوفيعلتمنب.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابفعلمنفوعلتمنقلتوفيعلتمنب.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابفعلمنفوعلتمنقلتوفيعلتمنب.claim: The full forms افعوعلت and افعاللت retain their long vowels; shortening would delete them to avoid two adjacent quiescent letters.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابفعلمنفوعلتمنقلتوفيعلتمنب.anchor: لو أسكنوا كان فيه حذف الألف والواو

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابفعلمنفوعلتمنقلتوفيعلتمنب.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابفعلمنفوعلتمنقلتوفيعلتمنب.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابفعلمنفوعلتمنقلتوفيعلتمنب.claim: Defective roots produce forms such as اقوولت, اسواددت, and ابياضضت.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابفعلمنفوعلتمنقلتوفيعلتمنب.anchor: اسواددت وابياضضت فإذا أردت فعل قلت

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابفعلمنفوعلتمنقلتوفيعلتمنب.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابفعلمنفوعلتمنقلتوفيعلتمنب.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابفعلمنفوعلتمنقلتوفيعلتمنب.claim: Examples of افعللت from defective roots include ازوررت and ابيضضت.

SAMIN-DURR:36:69/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:36:69/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:36:69/r1.claim: هو may refer to the Quran, indicated by context, or to knowledge, indicated by وما علمناه.
SAMIN-DURR:36:69/r1.anchor: قوله: { إن هو }: أي: إن القرآن. دل عليه السياق أو إن العلم إلا ذكر، يدل عليه: " وما علمناه "

SAMIN-DURR:36:69/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:36:69/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:36:69/r2.claim: The pronoun له may refer either to the Prophet or to the Quran.
SAMIN-DURR:36:69/r2.anchor: والضمير في " له " للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم. وقيل: للقرآن.

ASAD-NOTES:36:69#n38/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:36:69#n38/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:36:69#n38/r1.claim: This passage resumes the sūra's opening theme of Quranic revelation.
ASAD-NOTES:36:69#n38/r1.anchor: This passage resumes the theme enunciated in the opening verses of this surah, namely, the revelation of the Qur'an.

ASAD-NOTES:36:69#n38/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:36:69#n38/r2.speaker: Muhammad's opponents
ASAD-NOTES:36:69#n38/r2.claim: Muhammad's opponents, both in his time and later, alleged that his claimed revelation was invented as poetry; Asad links this allegation to 26:224.
ASAD-NOTES:36:69#n38/r2.anchor: the allegation of Muhammad's opponents, in his own as well as in later times, that what he described as divine revelation was in reality

ASAD-NOTES:36:69#n38/r3.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:36:69#n38/r3.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:36:69#n38/r3.claim: Asad distinguishes poetry, where meaning often serves rhythm and melody, from Quranic revelation, where wording, sound, position, rhythm, and melody serve intended meaning.
ASAD-NOTES:36:69#n38/r3.anchor: whereas in the former the meaning is often subordinated to the rhythm and the melody of language, in the Qur'an the exact opposite is the case

ASAD-NOTES:36:69#n39/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:36:69#n39/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:36:69#n39/r1.claim: Asad's composite rendering of mubin is clear in itself and clearly showing the truth; he refers to 12:2, note 2.
ASAD-NOTES:36:69#n39/r1.anchor: For this composite rendering of the adjective mubin, see surah 12, note 2.

ASAD-NOTES:36:69#n39/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:36:69#n39/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:36:69#n39/r2.claim: The conjunction wa, as at 15:1, marks the Quran as an integral element in the process of divine revelation.
ASAD-NOTES:36:69#n39/r2.anchor: with the conjunctive particle wa ("and") being used here, as in 15:1, to point out that the Qur'an is an integral element

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p53/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p53/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p53/r1.claim: The Prophet's denial of poetic authorship is not condemnation of poetry, as al-Bāqillānī suggests; poetry could be confused with the Qur'an's eloquent miracle because of its power over Arab feeling and thought.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p53/r1.anchor: حرص القرآن على أن ينفي عن المصطفى عليه الصلاة والسلام هذه الشاعرية، لا ذمًّا للشعر كما ذهب الباقلانى

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p53/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p53/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p53/r2.claim: The verse defines the Qur'an's nature and mission; later Meccan passages answer accusations that the Prophet is a poet or madman, in al-Ṣāffāt, al-Anbiyāʾ, and al-Ṭūr.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p53/r2.anchor: ونص الآية صريح في أنها تحديد لصفة القرآن وبيان لمهمته ورسالته، وليست إعلاناً عن موقف عداء للشعر

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p49/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p49/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p49/r1.claim: The opponents meant that the Qur'an's effect resembled poetry, not that its lines followed poetic meter.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p49/r1.anchor: وما نعلم المشركين خاضوا أيام المبعث، في أن من آيات القرآن ما يمكن أن يُحمل على وزن الشعر ونسقه

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p49/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p49/r2.speaker: أكثر أهل صناعة العربية
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p49/r2.claim: Al-Bāqillānī reports that the majority reject a single metrical line as poetry and require at least two lines.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p49/r2.anchor: البيت الواحد وما كان على وزنه لا يكون شعراً. وأقل الشعر بيتان فصاعداً

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p49/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p49/r3.speaker: العلماء
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p49/r3.claim: The cited scholars say two lines with differing meters or rhymes do not make a poem.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p49/r3.anchor: ما كان على وزن بيتين إلا إنه يختلف وزنهما أو قافيتهما فبيس شعر

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p49/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p49/r4.speaker: بعضهم
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p49/r4.claim: Some say rajaz is not poetry, especially in incomplete or short forms.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p49/r4.anchor: ثم منهم من قال إن الرجز ليس بشعر أصلاً، لاسيما إذا كان مشطوراً أو منهوكاً

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p49/r5.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p49/r5.speaker: الباقلاني
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p49/r5.claim: Al-Bāqillānī says poetry requires deliberate poetic method; Bint al-Shāṭiʾ finds this reply weaker because the same effects can occur in ordinary speech.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p49/r5.anchor: إن الشعر إنما يطلق متى قصد القاصد إليه على الطريق الذي يُتعمد ويُسلك

NASHR:v1p36/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p36/r1.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p36/r1.claim: The presence of weak or anomalous readings in these works did not lead scholars to deny their use in written attestations or to call them contrary to the seven aḥruf.
NASHR:v1p36/r1.anchor: ذلك على ما فيه من ضعيف وشاذ عن السبعة والعشرة وغيرهم فلا نعلم أحدا أنكر ذلك

NASHR:v1p36/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p36/r2.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p36/r2.claim: The author rejects the claim that only the readings of the seven canonical readers are sound or that those seven are the seven aḥruf mentioned by the Prophet.
NASHR:v1p36/r2.anchor: وإنما أطلنا هذا الفصل لما بلغنا عن بعض من لا علم له أن القراءات الصحيحة هي التي عن هؤلاء السبعة

NASHR:v1p36/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p36/r3.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p36/r3.claim: Some people treat the readings in al-Shāṭibiyya and al-Taysīr as exhaustive and label readings outside those books or the seven readers anomalous; the author notes some excluded readings are more authentic than included ones.
NASHR:v1p36/r3.anchor: وربما كان كثير مما لم يكن في الشاطبية والتيسير وعن غير هؤلاء السبعة أصح من كثير مما فيهما

NASHR:v1p36/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p36/r4.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p36/r4.claim: The confusion arose because people conflated the report of seven aḥruf with the seven readers’ names.
NASHR:v1p36/r4.anchor: كونهم سمعوا: أنزل القرآن على سبعة أحرف، وسمعوا قراءات السبعة

NASHR:v1p36/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p36/r5.speaker: الأئمة المتقدمون
NASHR:v1p36/r5.claim: Many early imams criticized Ibn Mujāhid for restricting his selection to seven and urged him to choose fewer or more readers, or explain his purpose, to prevent confusion.
NASHR:v1p36/r5.anchor: ولذلك كره كثير من الأئمة المتقدمين اقتصار ابن مجاهد على سبعة من القراء وخطئوه في ذلك

NASHR:v1p36/r6.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p36/r6.speaker: أحمد بن عمار المهدوي
NASHR:v1p36/r6.claim: Al-Mahdawī says later scholars selected the seven common regional readers for brevity and examination, but the public wrongly treated this choice as binding and condemned other readings.
NASHR:v1p36/r6.anchor: قال الإمام أبو العباس أحمد بن عمار المهدوي) : فأما اقتصار أهل الأمصار في الأغلب

NASHR:v1p36/r7.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p36/r7.speaker: أحمد بن عمار المهدوي
NASHR:v1p36/r7.claim: Later readers narrowed each imam to two transmitters, causing people to reject other transmissions even when those were more famous; he blames the seven-reader selection for public confusion.
NASHR:v1p36/r7.anchor: ثم اقتصر من قلت عنايته على راويين لكل إمام منهم، فصار إذا سمع قراءة راو عنه غيرهما أبطلها وربما كانت أشهر

QIRAAT-ER:36:69:14#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:36:69:14#1/r1.speaker: hmz
QIRAAT-ER:36:69:14#1/r1.claim: The hamza-less qurān reading is linked by the source to root q-r-y, “gather,” rather than q-r-ʾ, “read,” shifting emphasis from recitation to compilation.
QIRAAT-ER:36:69:14#1/r1.anchor: hmz, mutawatir: "Canonical variant without hamza: qurān instead of qur'ān -- removes the glottal stop

IBNHISHAM:v2p493/r1.author: Ibn Hishām
IBNHISHAM:v2p493/r1.speaker: عباس بن مرداس
IBNHISHAM:v2p493/r1.claim: ʿAbbās ibn Mirdās complains that he helped win and guard the spoils but received only four young camels, while Ḥuṣayn and Ḥābis received more despite not surpassing him.
IBNHISHAM:v2p493/r1.anchor: فقال عباس بن مرداس يعاتب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: كانت نهابا تلافيتها

IBNHISHAM:v2p493/r2.author: Ibn Hishām
IBNHISHAM:v2p493/r2.speaker: يونس النحوي
IBNHISHAM:v2p493/r2.claim: Yūnus al-Naḥwī transmits a variant of the poem’s line: it names Mirdās as the one whom Ḥuṣayn and Ḥābis did not surpass.
IBNHISHAM:v2p493/r2.anchor: قال ابن هشام: أنشدني يونس النحوي

IBNHISHAM:v2p493/r3.author: Ibn Hishām
IBNHISHAM:v2p493/r3.speaker: ابن إسحاق
IBNHISHAM:v2p493/r3.claim: When the Prophet ordered that Mirdās’s tongue be cut, he meant that he should be given enough to satisfy him; the gifts figuratively cut his tongue.
IBNHISHAM:v2p493/r3.anchor: فقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: اذهبوا به، فاقطعوا عني لسانه، فأعطوه حتى رضي

IBNHISHAM:v2p493/r4.author: Ibn Hishām
IBNHISHAM:v2p493/r4.speaker: أبو بكر الصديق
IBNHISHAM:v2p493/r4.claim: In another report, Abū Bakr corrects Mirdās’s ordering of the names al-Aqraʿ and ʿUyayna; the Prophet says they amount to the same, and Abū Bakr cites the verse that God did not teach him poetry.
IBNHISHAM:v2p493/r4.anchor: فقال أبو بكر الصديق: بين عيينة والأقرع، فقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: هما واحد

IBNHISHAM:v1p180/r1.author: Ibn Hishām
IBNHISHAM:v1p180/r1.speaker: ابن إسحاق
IBNHISHAM:v1p180/r1.claim: According to the report, Abū Ṭālib took the young Muhammad with a trading caravan to Syria; at Busra the monk Buḥayrā, custodian of inherited Christian book knowledge, lived in a hermitage.
IBNHISHAM:v1p180/r1.anchor: قال ابن إسحاق: ثم إن أبا طالب خرج في ركب تاجرا إلى الشام، فلما تهيأ للرحيل

IBNHISHAM:v1p180/r2.author: Ibn Hishām
IBNHISHAM:v1p180/r2.speaker: ابن إسحاق
IBNHISHAM:v1p180/r2.claim: Buḥayrā reportedly saw a cloud shade Muhammad and the branches of a tree bend over him; he descended and prepared a meal for the whole caravan, having often seen Quraysh pass without speaking to them.
IBNHISHAM:v1p180/r2.anchor: وكانوا كثيرا ما يمرون به قبل ذلك فلا يكلمهم ولا يعرض لهم حتى كان ذلك العام

IBNHISHAM:v1p180/r3.author: Ibn Hishām
IBNHISHAM:v1p180/r3.speaker: ابن إسحاق
IBNHISHAM:v1p180/r3.claim: When the young Muhammad stayed with the baggage and Buḥayrā could not see the identifying sign he sought, the monk insisted he join the meal; a Quraysh man objected that leaving him out would be shameful.
IBNHISHAM:v1p180/r3.anchor: فلما نظر بحيرى في القوم لم ير الصفة التي يعرف ويجد عنده، فقال: يا معشر قريش

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p145#5/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p145#5/r1.speaker: عائشة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p145#5/r1.claim: Aisha said poetry was the Prophet’s most disliked speech, and that his sole attempt at Tarafa’s verse changed its final words; Abu Bakr corrected him, and the Prophet said he was no poet.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p145#5/r1.anchor: عن معمر عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ وما علمناه الشعر ﴾ قال بلغني أن عائشة سئلت هل كان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يتمثل بشيء من الشعر

MUSLIM:6362/r1.author: MUSLIM
MUSLIM:6362/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
MUSLIM:6362/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas reports Abu Dharr’s brother described Muhammad as commanding noble morals and speaking words that were not poetry, echoing the verse’s distinction between revelation and poetry.
MUSLIM:6362/r1.anchor: رأيته يأمر بمكارم الأخلاق وكلاما ما هو بالشعر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p80/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p80/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p80/r1.claim: The pronoun in علمناه refers to the Messenger, whom the opponents called a poet.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p80/r1.anchor: الضمير في علمناه للرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم، كانوا يقولون فيه شاعر.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p80/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p80/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p80/r2.claim: A report identifies ʿUqba b. Abī Muʿayṭ as the person who accused the Messenger of poetry; God refuted the charge.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p80/r2.anchor: وروي أن القائل عقبة بن أبي معيط، فنفى الله ذلك عنه، وقولهم فيه شاعر.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p80/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p80/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p80/r3.claim: If poetry came naturally to him, the charge was stubbornness meant to mislead the ignorant; if not, it was sheer ignorance.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p80/r3.anchor: أما من كان في طبعه الشعر، فقوله مكابرة وإيهام للجاهل بالشعر وأما من ليس في طبعه، فقوله جهل محض.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p80/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p80/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p80/r4.claim: Poetry is metrical, rhymed speech conveying a selected meaning through imaginative embellishment; the devout avoid reciting it, much less composing it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p80/r4.anchor: والشعر إنما هو كلام موزون مقفى يدل على معنى تنتخبه الشعراء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p80/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p80/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p80/r5.claim: The Prophet did not compose poetry; when he cited a line such as ستبدي لك الأيام ما كنت جاهلا, he conveyed its meaning without its meter.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p80/r5.anchor: وكان عليه السلام لا يقول الشعر، وإذا أنشد بيتا أحرز المعنى دون وزنه، كما أنشد:

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p80/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p80/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p80/r6.claim: An anecdote says that when asked who was the most poetic, he answered by citing lines beginning ألم ترياني كلما جئت طارقا and أتجعل نهبي ونهب العبيد.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p80/r6.anchor: وقيل: من أشعر الناس، فقال الذي يقول: ألم ترياني كلما جئت طارقا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p80/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p80/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p80/r7.claim: Once he uttered كفى بالإسلام والشيب ناهيا; Abū Bakr and ʿUmar testified he was God's Messenger, noting the poet's wording reverses its order, and he only rarely spoke in meter.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p80/r7.anchor: وأنشد يوما: كفى بالإسلام والشيب ناهيا فقال أبو بكر وعمر: نشهد أنك رسول الله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p80/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p80/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p80/r8.claim: A report has him reciting a line by Ibn Rawāḥa; its meter does not prove poetic knowledge, since he could utter it without intending meter.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p80/r8.anchor: وروي عنه أنشد بيت ابن رواحة: يبيت يجافي جنبه عن فراشه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p80/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p80/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p80/r9.claim: His metrical phrases, including أنا النبي لا كذب and هل أنت إلا أصبع دميت, arose naturally without craft, intent to meter, or effort.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p80/r9.anchor: وهو كلام من جنس كلامه الذي كان يتكلم به على طبيعته، من غير صنعة فيه ولا قصد لوزن ولا تكلف.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p80/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p80/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p80/r10.claim: The Qur'an can contain metrically shaped phrases without becoming poetry; Abū Ḥayyān cites 3:92 and 18:29, as well as eloquent prose.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p80/r10.anchor: كما يوجد في القرآن شيء موزون ولا يعد شعرا، كقوله تعالى:

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p80/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p80/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p80/r11.claim: وما ينبغي له means poetry is neither possible nor proper or fitting for the Messenger, whose path is serious, unlike poetry's usual frivolity, false embellishment, and excess.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p80/r11.anchor: وما ينبغي له: أي ولا يمكن له ولا يصح ولا يناسب، لأنه عليه السلام في طريق جد محض

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p80/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p80/r12.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p80/r12.claim: God made the Prophet unable to compose poetry, just as He made him unable to write, strengthening the proof and dispelling suspicion.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p80/r12.anchor: جعله تعالى لا يقرض الشعر، كما جعله أميا لا يخط، لتكون الحجة أثبت والشبهة أدحض.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p80/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p80/r13.speaker: قوم
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p80/r13.claim: Some say the verse implies that poetry is a debased or inferior art.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p80/r13.anchor: وقيل: في هذه الآية دلالة على غضاضة الشعر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p81/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p81/r1.speaker: الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p81/r1.claim: The Prophet said that he was not a poet and that poetry was not fitting for him.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p81/r1.anchor: وقد قال عليه السلام: «ما أنا بشاعر ولا ينبغي لي»

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p81/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p81/r2.speaker: قوم
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p81/r2.claim: Some hold poetry is no disgrace and that God barred His Prophet from this noble adornment so the Qur'an would seem more extraordinary; otherwise it could be attributed to poetic skill.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p81/r2.anchor: وذهب قوم إلى أنه لا غضاضة فيه، وإنما منعه الله نبيه عليه الصلاة والسلام. وإن كان حلية جليلة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p81/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p81/r3.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p81/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya rejects that explanation: the Prophet already had the highest eloquence in prose, while God's speech is distinguished by inimitability and divine knowledge.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p81/r3.anchor: قال ابن عطية: وليس الأمر عندي كذلك، وقد كان عليه السلام من الفصاحة والبيان في النثر في الرتبة العليا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p81/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p81/r4.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p81/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya says God prevented the Prophet from poetry to elevate him above poets' imaginative invention and verbal ornamentation.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p81/r4.anchor: وإنما منع الله نبيه من الشعر ترفيعا له عن ما في قول الشعراء من التخييل والتزويق للقول.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p81/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p81/r5.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p81/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya describes the Qur'an as remembrance of truths and proofs, not a poet's speech, and says this was the Prophet's consistent manner of speaking.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p81/r5.anchor: وأما القرآن فهو ذكر بحقائق وبراهين، فما هو بقول شاعر، وهذا كان أسلوب كلامه، عليه السلام

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p81/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p81/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p81/r6.claim: The pronoun in له refers to the Messenger; Abū Ḥayyān calls the alternative that it refers to the Qur'an remote, though the context can support it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p81/r6.anchor: والضمير في له للرسول، أي وما ينبغي الشعر لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم. وأبعد من ذهب إلى أنه عائد على القرآن

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p81/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p81/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p81/r7.claim: The Qur'an is a heavenly book recited in prayer niches; reciting and acting on it brings felicity in both worlds, unlike poetry, mostly satanic prompting.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p81/r7.anchor: أي كتاب سماوي يقرأ في المحاريب، وينال بتلاوته والعمل به ما فيه فوز الدارين.

ALUSI-FULL:v23p46#3/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p46#3/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p46#3/r1.claim: God did not teach the Prophet poetry through the Qurʾān, whose eloquent teaching clarifies and distinguishes matters of origin and return.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p46#3/r1.anchor: بتعليم الكتاب المشتمل على هذا البيان والتخليص في أمر المبدأ والمعاد

ALUSI-FULL:v23p46#3/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p46#3/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p46#3/r2.claim: The Qurʾān differs from poetry in sound because it has neither meter nor rhyme, and in meaning because poetry relies on imaginative evocation while the Qurʾān gives judgments, beliefs, and laws.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p46#3/r2.anchor: أما لفظا فلعدم وزنه وتقفيته وأما معنى فلأن الشعر تخيلات مرغبة أو منفرة أو نحو ذلك

ALUSI-FULL:v23p46#3/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p46#3/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p46#3/r3.claim: The denial that God taught him poetry indirectly denies that the Qurʾān is poetry: what God taught is the Qurʾān, and what was taught was not poetry.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p46#3/r3.anchor: والمراد من نفي تعليمه صلى الله عليه وسلم بتعليم الكتاب الشعر نفي أن يكون القرآن شعرا

ALUSI-FULL:v23p46#3/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p46#3/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p46#3/r4.claim: The statement also implies that the Prophet is no poet; al-Ālūsī rejects the claim that this is merely an oblique allusion.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p46#3/r4.anchor: وفيه أنه عليه الصلاة والسلام ليس بشاعر إدماجا وليس هناك كناية تلويحية كما قيل

ALUSI-FULL:v23p46#3/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p46#3/r5.speaker: القائلون من الكفار
ALUSI-FULL:v23p46#3/r5.claim: The opponents called the Qurʾān poetry and the Prophet a poet to portray his revelation as fabrication and imaginative fancy; al-Ālūsī rejects this charge.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p46#3/r5.anchor: وهذا رد لما كانوا يقولونه من أن القرآن شعر والنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم شاعر

ALUSI-FULL:v23p46#3/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p46#3/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p46#3/r6.claim: The parenthetical phrase confirms that poetry is unfitting for the Prophet: meter can force altered meanings, while exaggeration and distortion in poetry invite falsehood.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p46#3/r6.anchor: لأنه يدعو إلى تغيير المعنى لمراعاة اللفظ والوزن ولأن أحسنه المبالغة والمجازفة والإغراق في الوصف

ALUSI-FULL:v23p47/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p47/r1.speaker: ابن الحاجب
ALUSI-FULL:v23p47/r1.claim: Ibn al-Ḥājib argues that it would be irrational for the Prophet to compose poetry, since people might suspect revelation came from his own poetic faculty; removal of doubt leaves only their obstinacy, so the judgment falls on disbelievers.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p47/r1.anchor: وقال ابن الحاجب : أي لا يستقيم عقلا أن يقول صلى الله عليه وسلم الشعر لأنه لو كان ممن يقوله

ALUSI-FULL:v23p47/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p47/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p47/r2.claim: Al-Ālūsī objects that eloquent prose could prompt suspicion as much as poetry, yet the Prophet was not barred from eloquence; the miracle itself removes reasonable doubt, so Ibn al-Ḥājib's cause is insufficient.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p47/r2.anchor: فلو كانت علة منعه عليه الصلاة والسلام من الشعر ما ذكر لزم أن يمنع من الكلام الفصيح البليغ

ALUSI-FULL:v23p47/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p47/r3.speaker: ابن عطية
ALUSI-FULL:v23p47/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya locates the reason in poetry's imaginative ornamentation and embellishment; al-Ālūsī says this is the sound explanation to rely on.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p47/r3.anchor: واختار هذا ابن عطية وجعل العلة ما في قول الشعر من التخييل والتزويق للقول

ALUSI-FULL:v23p47/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p47/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p47/r4.claim: The verse indicates poetry's low standing in this context and that the Prophet lacked a poetic disposition, honoring him and distancing him from anything that could impair prophetic dignity.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p47/r4.anchor: وفي الآية عليه دلالة على غضاضة الشعر وهي ظاهرة في أنه عليه الصلاة والسلام لم يعط طبيعة شعرية

ALUSI-FULL:v23p47/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p47/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p47/r5.claim: Not giving the Prophet poetic ability, while also preserving him from composing poetry, removes a capacity that might harm his exalted office, by analogy with infallibility and protection.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p47/r5.anchor: وإنما لم يعط صلى الله عليه وسلم القدرة على الشعر مع حفظه عن إنشائه لأن ذلك سلب القدرة عليه

ALUSI-FULL:v23p47/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p47/r6.speaker: بعض الناس
ALUSI-FULL:v23p47/r6.claim: Some infer from al-Mawāhib al-ladunniyya that the Prophet could compose poetry but was forbidden to do so; al-Ālūsī rejects this account.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p47/r6.anchor: ويفهم من كلام المواهب اللدنية أن من الناس من ذهب إلى أنه عليه الصلاة والسلام كان له قدرة على الشعر

ALUSI-FULL:v23p47/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p47/r7.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v23p47/r7.claim: Some hold the denial applies to all prophets because the verse gives no apparent reason to restrict it to Muḥammad; another view allows it to be particular to him as added honor.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p47/r7.anchor: وهل عدم الشعر خاص به عليه الصلاة والسلام أو عام لنوع الأنبياء قال بعضهم هو عام لهذه الآية

ALUSI-FULL:v23p47/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p47/r8.speaker: قائلون
ALUSI-FULL:v23p47/r8.claim: Those who make the denial specific to Muḥammad say other prophets could retain poetic ability while being protected from composing poetry; this account treats the distinction as extra honor for him.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p47/r8.anchor: وقيل بحوز أن يكون خاصا والنكتة زيادة التكريم لما أن مقامه صلى الله عليه وسلم فوق مقام الأنبياء

ALUSI-FULL:v23p47/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p47/r9.speaker: آدم عليه السلام
ALUSI-FULL:v23p47/r9.claim: If the report that Adam composed verses when his son was killed is authentic, it supports the view that the denial of poetic ability was particular to Muḥammad.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p47/r9.anchor: وإن صح خبر إنشاء آدم عليه السلام يوم قتل ولده

ALUSI-FULL:v23p48/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p48/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p48/r1.claim: The Prophet's spontaneous, accidentally metrical words at Ḥunayn do not make him a poet, since poetry is deliberately composed metered and rhyming speech; such rhythms can occur in prose.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p48/r1.anchor: فقد عرفوه بأنه الكلام المقفى الموزون على سبيل القصد وهذا مما اتفق له عليه الصلاة والسلام

ALUSI-FULL:v23p48/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p48/r2.speaker: قوم
ALUSI-FULL:v23p48/r2.claim: Some do not classify rajaz as poetry at all; al-Khalīl defines its base form as six mustafʿilun feet and calls its performer a rājiz rather than a poet.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p48/r2.anchor: ما كان على مستفعلن ست مرات شعرا ولذا يسمى قائله راجزا

ALUSI-FULL:v23p48/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p48/r3.speaker: الخليل
ALUSI-FULL:v23p48/r3.claim: One account from al-Khalīl excludes the half-form (mashṭūr) and shortened form (manhūk) of rajaz from poetry; another excludes the four-foot majzūʾ form too.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p48/r3.anchor: وعن الخليل أن المشطور منه وهو ما حذف نصفه فبقي وزنه مستفعلن ثلاث مرات والمنهوك

ALUSI-FULL:v23p48/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p48/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p48/r4.claim: The alternative claim that the pronoun in 'is not fitting for him' refers to the Qurʾān is unsound: the preceding denial already excludes poetry from the Prophet, and the pronoun naturally refers to him.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p48/r4.anchor: فإنه يكفي في نفي الشعر عنه عليه الصلاة والسلام

ALUSI-FULL:v23p48/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p48/r5.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
ALUSI-FULL:v23p48/r5.claim: At Ḥunayn the Prophet recited Ibn Rawāḥa's line about lying awake while the polytheists sleep; this is an instance of quoting metrical speech, not composing poetry.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p48/r5.anchor: وإنشاده إياه كذلك مذكور في البحر

ALUSI-FULL:v23p48/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p48/r6.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
ALUSI-FULL:v23p48/r6.claim: A report says that after a finger was hurt in battle the Prophet recited a line about the injured finger and service in God's path; Ibn Hishām attributes it to al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīra, while Ibn al-Jawzī prefers Ibn Rawāḥa.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p48/r6.anchor: أو ابن رواحة على ما صححه ابن الجوزي

ALUSI-FULL:v23p49/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p49/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
ALUSI-FULL:v23p49/r1.claim: In a report, the Prophet quoted Ṭarafa's line that the days will reveal what one does not know and bring news from one not sent to ask; Abū Bakr corrected his wording, and he disclaimed being a poet.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p49/r1.anchor: ستبدي لك الأيام ما كنت جاهلا ويأتيك من لم تزود بالأخبار فقال أبو بكر رضي الله تعالى عنه ليس هكذا يا رسول الله

ALUSI-FULL:v23p49/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p49/r2.speaker: عائشة
ALUSI-FULL:v23p49/r2.claim: Aḥmad and Ibn Abī Shayba transmit from ʿĀʾisha that when awaiting news, the Prophet would quote Ṭarafa's line ending 'news from one not sent to ask.'
ALUSI-FULL:v23p49/r2.anchor: إذا استراث الخبر تمثل ببيت طرفة

ALUSI-FULL:v23p49/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p49/r3.speaker: الحسن
ALUSI-FULL:v23p49/r3.claim: Ibn Saʿd and Ibn Abī Ḥātim transmit from al-Ḥasan that the Prophet quoted the line 'Islam and gray hair suffice to admonish a man'; Abū Bakr took it as proof he was not taught poetry.

ALUSI-FULL:v23p49/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p49/r4.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن أبي الزناد
ALUSI-FULL:v23p49/r4.claim: Ibn Saʿīd transmits from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī al-Zinād that the Prophet corrected al-ʿAbbās ibn Mirdās's verse order; Abū Bakr said he was neither poet nor poetry-reciter.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p49/r4.anchor: وأخرج ابن سعيد عن عبد الرحمن بن أبي الزناد أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال للعباس بن مرداس

ALUSI-FULL:v23p49/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p49/r5.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
ALUSI-FULL:v23p49/r5.claim: Asked who the greatest poet is, the Prophet reportedly cited the poet who says that whenever he comes at night, he finds perfume there even if he brought none.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p49/r5.anchor: وروي أنه قيل له عليه الصلاة والسلام : من أشعر الناس فقال : الذي يقول : ألم ترياني كلما جئت طارقا

ALUSI-FULL:v23p49/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p49/r6.speaker: عائشة
ALUSI-FULL:v23p49/r6.claim: Al-Bayhaqī transmits from ʿĀʾisha, through a chain with an unknown narrator, that the Prophet never assembled a full verse except the aphorism about what one hopes for; she says he avoided its final inflection lest it become a poem.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p49/r6.anchor: وأخرج البيهقي في سننه بسند فيه مجهول عن عائشة قالت ما جمع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بيت شعر قط إلا بيتا واحدا

ALUSI-FULL:v23p49/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p49/r7.speaker: عائشة
ALUSI-FULL:v23p49/r7.claim: Aḥmad's Musnad reports from ʿĀʾisha that poetry was the Prophet's most disliked speech.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p49/r7.anchor: ففي مسند أحمد بن حنبل عن عائشة قالت : كان أبغض الحديث إليه صلى الله عليه وسلم الشعر

ALUSI-FULL:v23p49/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p49/r8.speaker: أبو هريرة
ALUSI-FULL:v23p49/r8.claim: In the two Ṣaḥīḥs and other collections, the Prophet says a person's stomach being full of pus is better than being full of poetry; al-Ālūsī reads this as censuring excessive poetry.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p49/r8.anchor: وفي الصحيحين وغيرهما عن أبي هريرة أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال لأن يمتليء جوف أحدكم قيحا خير له

ALUSI-FULL:v23p49/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p49/r9.speaker: الخليل
ALUSI-FULL:v23p49/r9.claim: Al-Khalīl is also reported to say poetry was dearer to the Prophet than much speech; al-Ālūsī reconciles this with ʿĀʾisha's report by distinguishing kinds of poetry.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p49/r9.anchor: وما روي عن الخليل أنه قال كان الشعر أحب إلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم من كثير من الكلام

ALUSI-FULL:v23p49/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p49/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p49/r10.claim: The Qurʾān is an admonition from God and guidance for both humans and jinn, as the phrase 'a reminder for all the worlds' also says.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p49/r10.anchor: أي عظة من الله عز وجل وإرشاد للثقلين

ALUSI-FULL:v23p49#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p49#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p49#2/r1.claim: It is a manifest heavenly book, plainly not human speech because its inimitability silences those who challenge it.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p49#2/r1.anchor: أي كتاب سماوي ظاهر أنه ليس من كلام البشر لما فيه من الإعجاز الذي ألقم من تصدى للمعارضة الحجر

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p27/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p27/r1.speaker: عائشة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p27/r1.claim: ʿĀʾisha says poetry was the Prophet's most disliked speech.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p27/r1.anchor: بلغني أن عائشة سئلت: هل كان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يتمثل بشيء من الشعر؟ قالت: كان الشعر أبغض الحديث إليه،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p27/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p27/r2.speaker: عائشة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p27/r2.claim: ʿĀʾisha reports that he recited only a line attributed to Ṭarafa, altered its wording, and was corrected by Abū Bakr.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p27/r2.anchor: ولم يتمثل بشيء من الشعر إلا ببيت أخي بني قيس طرفة: ستبدي لك الأيام ما كنت جاهلا

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p27/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p27/r3.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p27/r3.claim: After Abū Bakr corrected the line, the Prophet said he was not a poet and poetry was not fitting for him.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p27/r3.anchor: يا رسول الله، فقال: "إني لست بشاعر ولا ينبغي لي"

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p27/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p27/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p27/r4.claim: The Qur'an is admonition and a clear recitation containing obligations, legal limits, and rulings.

BIQAI-FULL:v6p279#2/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p279#2/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p279#2/r1.claim: Poetry's contrivance is far from prophetic nature; it is used for praise and blame and is mostly false, making it unfitting for the noblest prophet.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p279#2/r1.anchor: فكيف بأشرفهم مما يكتسب به مدحا وهجوا , فيكون أكثره كذبا

BIQAI-FULL:v6p279#2/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p279#2/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p279#2/r2.claim: Here, what is not fitting means what is neither proper nor sought nor possible for him, given his rank and high aspiration.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p279#2/r2.anchor: أي وما يصح ولا ينطلب ولا يتأتى أصلا

BIQAI-FULL:v6p279#2/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p279#2/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p279#2/r3.claim: Poetry deliberately follows a set meter and rhyme; those constraints force inversions and circumlocutions that obscure meaning and make it hard to understand.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p279#2/r3.anchor: أن الشعر - وهو تعمد صوغ الكلام على وزن معلوم وقافية ملتزمة - نقيصة

BIQAI-FULL:v6p279#2/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p279#2/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p279#2/r4.claim: The revelation is an honor and admonition, gathers wisdom for this life and the next, is recited in prayer, and brings success in both abodes through recitation and practice.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p279#2/r4.anchor: أي شرف وموعظة { وقرآن } أي جامع للحكم كلها دنيا وأخرى يتلى في المحاريب

BIQAI-FULL:v6p279#2/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p279#2/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p279#2/r5.claim: The Qur'an makes its contents manifest to anyone who truly seeks them, whether clever or dull; poetry, despite its lesser eloquence, admonishes only the very intelligent.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p279#2/r5.anchor: بعد أن يشترط في مطلق فهمه ومجرد اللذة به الذكي والغبي والحديد والبليد

BIQAI-FULL:v6p279#2/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p279#2/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p279#2/r6.claim: The ending of Sād clarifies that the Qur'an is a reminder for all people, clever and dull alike, whereas poetry is for the exceptionally intelligent.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p279#2/r6.anchor: ويبين هذا المعنى غاية البيان آخر ( ص )

BIQAI-FULL:v6p280/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p280/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p280/r7.claim: The Qur'an's governing aim is serious meaning, with words following it; poets and rhymers put rhyme and cadence first, which can produce weak or false meanings.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p280/r7.anchor: أن أعظم منافاة القرآن للشعر وكذا السجع من أجل أنه جد كله

BIQAI-FULL:v6p280/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p280/r8.speaker: حسان بن ثابت
BIQAI-FULL:v6p280/r8.claim: At the expedition of al-Ghāba, Ḥassān's rhyming verse angered Saʿd ibn Zayd al-Ashhalī, who gave his horses to al-Miqdād and swore not to speak to him; Ḥassān explained the rhyme had forced the name.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p280/r8.anchor: قال حسان بن ثابت رضي الله عنه وحاله معروف في البلاغة والتفنن في أساليب الكلام

BIQAI-FULL:v6p280/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p280/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p280/r9.claim: The Prophet never chooses wording merely for polish or meter; he avoids a metrical option when it fails to convey the intended meaning, just as Arabs avoid grammatical error because it is error.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p280/r9.anchor: فالنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم لا يدور في فكره أبدا قصد اللفظ

DURR-FULL:v7p71/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p71/r1.speaker: أبو بكر
DURR-FULL:v7p71/r1.claim: A report says the Prophet recited a verse that Islam and gray hair suffice to restrain a man; Abū Bakr said God had not taught him poetry and that poetry was unbecoming of him.
DURR-FULL:v7p71/r1.anchor: أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كان يتمثل بهذا البيت: كفى بالإسلام والشيب للمرء ناهيا فقال أبو بكر رضي الله عنه

DURR-FULL:v7p71/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p71/r2.speaker: أبو بكر
DURR-FULL:v7p71/r2.claim: When the Prophet asked al-ʿAbbās ibn Mirdās about a verse describing booty, Abū Bakr corrected the word order and said the Prophet was neither poet nor reciter.
DURR-FULL:v7p71/r2.anchor: عن عبد الرحمن بن أبي الزناد رضي الله عنه أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال للعباس بن مرداس: أرأيت قولك

DURR-FULL:v7p71/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p71/r3.speaker: عائشة
DURR-FULL:v7p71/r3.claim: ʿĀʾishah says the Prophet never completed a line of poetry except one; the report's chain contains a narrator of unknown status, and she advises wording that would not scan as poetry.
DURR-FULL:v7p71/r3.anchor: عن عائشة رضي الله عنها قالت: ما جمع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بيت شعر قط إلا بيتا واحدا

DURR-FULL:v7p71/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p71/r4.speaker: رسول الله
DURR-FULL:v7p71/r4.claim: The Prophet says he does not care what he does if he drinks theriac, wears an amulet, or composes poetry himself.
DURR-FULL:v7p71/r4.anchor: عن ابن عمرو رضي الله عنه سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول: ما أبالي ما أتيت إن أنا شربت ترياقا

DURR-FULL:v7p71/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p71/r6.speaker: عائشة
DURR-FULL:v7p71/r6.claim: Asked whether poetry was heard in the Prophet's presence, ʿĀʾishah said it was the speech he disliked most.
DURR-FULL:v7p71/r6.anchor: عن نوفل بن عقرب قال: سألت عائشة رضي الله عنها هل كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يتسامع عنده الشعر

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3200#2/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3200#2/r1.speaker: السدي
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3200#2/r1.claim: Al-Suddi identifies the person whom God did not teach poetry as Muhammad.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3200#2/r1.anchor: عن السدى رضي الله ، عنه في قوله : وما علمنا الشعر قال : محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3200#2/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3200#2/r2.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3200#2/r2.claim: Qatada says Muhammad was protected from poetry; the reminder is the Quran, intended to warn the living, meaning those alive in heart and sight, while the word takes effect against unbelievers through their evil deeds.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3200#2/r2.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله : وما علمناه الشعر وما ينبغي له قال : محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم ، عصمه الله من ذلك

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3200#2/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3200#2/r3.speaker: عائشة
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3200#2/r3.claim: Aisha says poetry was the Prophet’s most disliked speech, though he would sometimes quote a line from a man of Banu Qays with its halves reversed; when Abu Bakr corrected it, the Prophet said he was not a poet and poetry did not befit him.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3200#2/r3.anchor: بلغني انه قيل لعائشة رضي الله ، عنها هل كان رسول الله يتمثل بشيء من الشعر ؟ قالت : كان ابغض الحديث اليه غير انه كان يتمثل ببيت اخي بني قيس

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3200#2/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3200#2/r4.speaker: الحسن البصري
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3200#2/r4.claim: Hasan al-Basri reports that the Prophet quoted a verse about Islam and gray hair; Abu Bakr corrected its word order, after which Abu Bakr or Umar affirmed that he was God’s Messenger.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3200#2/r4.anchor: حدثنا أبي حدثنا أبو سلمة حدثنا حماد بن سلمة ، عن علي بن زيد ، عن الحسن هو البصري قال : ان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كان يتمثل بهذا البيت

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p461/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p461/r1.speaker: الحسن بن أبي الحسن
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p461/r1.claim: Al-Ḥasan reports that the Prophet recited a line about Islam and old age; Abū Bakr and ʿUmar corrected its wording, showing that a metrically sound recitation did not make him a poet.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p461/r1.anchor: وقال الحسن بن أبي الحسن: أنشد النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم «كفى بالإسلام والشيب للمرء ناهيا»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p461/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p461/r2.speaker: عائشة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p461/r2.claim: ʿĀʾisha says poetry was the Prophet's most disliked speech; when he misquoted a line by Ṭarafa, Abū Bakr corrected him, and he said he was no poet and should not be one.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p461/r2.anchor: قول عائشة رضي الله عنها: كان الشعر أبغض الحديث إلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p461/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p461/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p461/r3.claim: Occasionally hitting a poetic meter does not show that the Prophet knew poetry; prose can also fall into meter, as in his saying at Ḥunayn, “I am the Prophet, no lie; I am the son of ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib.”
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p461/r3.anchor: وإصابته الوزن أحيانا لا يوجب أنه يعلم الشعر، وكذلك قد يأتي أحيانا في نثر كلامه ما يدخل في وزن

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p461/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p461/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p461/r4.claim: He reads the verse as necessarily disparaging poetry.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p461/r4.anchor: وهذه الآية تقتضي عندي غضاضة على الشعر ولا بد

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p461/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p461/r5.speaker: قوم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p461/r5.claim: Some say poetry itself is not blameworthy; God withheld this adornment from the Prophet so the Qur'an would be more extraordinary, since poetic skill could otherwise be alleged as its source.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p461/r5.anchor: وقد ذهب قوم إلى أن الشعر لا غض عليه، قالوا وإنما منعه الله من التحلي بهذه الحلية الرفيعة ليجيء القرآن من قبله أغرب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p461/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p461/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p461/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya rejects that explanation: the Prophet had the highest eloquence in prose, while the Qur'an's arrangement and encompassing divine knowledge make its inimitability clear.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p461/r6.anchor: وليس الأمر عندي كذلك، وقد كان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم من الفصاحة والبيان في النثر في المرتبة العليا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p461/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p461/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p461/r7.claim: God kept the Prophet from poetry to raise him above poets' imaginative embellishment; the Qur'an conveys truths and proofs, and the Prophet's speech follows that model because he does not speak from whim.
